prompt: Create an original editorial illustration for the Start Here opening of Code Like It's 198x, a website where beginners explore programming, games and computing history. A wide full-bleed panorama, about 3:1. It should feel like being invited to open an imaginative making kit, not a desk full of expert debugging equipment. Compose a shallow open cardboard tray partly beyond the right edge, with tactile cut-paper and small wooden pieces spreading joyfully out of it: chunky bright pixel squares, a few simple abstract game counters, folded paper surfaces with faint abstract marks, and one modest anonymous cream keyboard corner. The pieces are beginning to form a loose playful little game space; leave their meaning open rather than demonstrating a real program or a prescribed learning sequence. Reserve the left third as calm, softly lit warm off-white paper for a later live Start Here heading. Let a few large pieces overlap the implied boundary of that quiet area without obstructing it. Strong three-dimensional material quality, crisp cut edges, beautiful warm directional light and physical cast shadows. Restrained but cheerful coral, golden yellow, teal and deep blue pieces against warm cream and charcoal. Contemporary printed editorial craft with energy and generous space, not vintage sepia nostalgia or an exploded engineering diagram. No magnifying glass, tangled wire or oscilloscope graphs; this must feel welcoming and different from an investigation workbench. No people, logos, identifiable commercial hardware or characters. No writing, titles, code, labels, arrows, literal pathway/map, UI cards or frame. All objects deliberately imagined original illustration, not historical or technical evidence.
